metadata.title: chore: standardize cargo-deny coverage for rust projects
metadata.author: lucarlig

description:
## 🔗 Related Issue
Closes #3743

---

## 📝 Summary
Standardizes `cargo-deny` coverage across the repo's standalone Rust projects and adds explicit CI enforcement for Rust plugin workflows.

This updates the Rust tools workflow to use a dedicated `make deny` path, adds a root `make rust-deny` target for Rust plugins, and checks in the canonical `deny.toml` to each Rust project that needs it. It also adds the missing license field in the filesystem Rust server so `cargo-deny` passes cleanly.

---

reviews.author: crivetimihai
reviews.body:
Reviewed and rebased onto main (clean, no conflicts). Added two review-driven commits on top of the original:

**1. CI coverage for `mcp_runtime`** — Added `cargo deny check licenses bans sources` step in `rust-tools.yml` for `tools_rust/mcp_runtime`, which had a `deny.toml` but no CI enforcement. Advisories excluded due to pre-existing failures (`aws-lc-sys`, `rustls-webpki`, `rustls-pemfile`) tracked separately.

**2. Trimmed license allowlist + mcp-servers CI coverage:**
- Reduced `deny.toml` allowlist from 107 licenses to 17 (14 actually in use + 3 safe buffer). Removed problematic licenses never needed by any dependency (`JSON`, `CDDL-*`, `EPL-*`, `BSD-4-Clause`, `MPL-*`, `SISSL-*`, etc.).
- Added `cargo deny check licenses bans sources` CI steps for `mcp-servers/rust/fast-test-server` and `mcp-servers/rust/filesystem-server` in `rust-tools.yml`, with path triggers for `mcp-servers/rust/**`.

All 7 Rust projects verified passing locally with the trimmed allowlist. `make rust-deny` and `make deny` (wrapper) both green.
